parties:
Bangladesh Garments Manufactures and Exporters Association and others ------- Petitioners.
Vs.
Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry & others ------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J : In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause why the impugned order dated 25-9-2007 (Annexure-A) passed by respondent No. 2 purporting to direct respondent No. 1 to exclude all five nominees of the petitioner from the voter's list of FBCCI for the FBCCI election 2007-2008 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in brief, are :

3. Petitioner No.1, Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913. Respondent No.1 is the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI) organised in fulfilment of the provisions of section 3(2)(a) of The Trade Organisations Ordinance, 1961 (in short, the Ordinance). Respondent No. 3 issued a notice of election dated 26-5-2007 to all the member bodies of FBCCI for election of its Board of Directors for the two years' term from 2007-2008 and 2008-2009 to be held on 16-8-2007. The member bodies of FBCCI were requested to send nominations of their representatives to the general body which would elect the Board of Directors. As an 'A' Class association, BGMEA was requested to nominate five representatives. Later, by a further notice of election dated 21-8-2007, respondent No. 3 deferred the election date to 20-11-2007 with a revised election schedule as evident in Annexure- "C", BGMEA submitted to the Election Board its nomination of five representatives to the General Body of FBCCI including petitioner No. 1 according to the form annexed to the notice of election as evident in Annexure-'D'.

4. On receipt of the nominations of the representatives from different member bodies, the Election Board of FBCCI published the preliminary voters' list on 25-6-2007 including the names of BGMEA nominees at serial No. 82 as voter Nos. 386 to 390. After publication of the preliminary voter list, one Mahbub Minhaj, respondent N. 6, submitted an objection dated 30-6-2007 to respondent No.4, that is, the Election Appeal Board, praying for disqualifying the nominated members of the present Executive Committee of BGMEA and from entering them as voters in FBCCI election of 2007-2008. According to him, the legal character and competency of holding the posts of the present Executive Committee was under challenge before the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 116 of 2007. In that suit an application was filed for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from holding BGMEA election of 2007-2008. During the pendency of the suit the plaintiff filed a further application and the learned Assistant Judge granted interim injunction on 22-2-2007 restraining holding of BGMEA election on 25-2-2007 till disposal of the suit. In violation of that order, the election was held on 25-2-2007. By an order dated 11-3-2007, the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka passed a temporary order of injunction on 11-3-2007 restraining the defendants from handing over the executive power and from holding the AGM (Annual General Meeting) of BGMEA. Against that order of injunction, defendant No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 84 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The Appeal was, however, allowed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka by his order dated 5-6-2007. BGMEA election was, however held as per the revised election schedule on 3-12-2007. After that, Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2007 filed by the plaintiff for violating the order of injunction dated 22-2-2007 has been pending for hearing. The order of injunction dated 11-3-2007 restraining the defendants from holding the AGM of BGMEA or transfer of executive power was not violated. Neither BGMEA nor any -of the members of its outgoing Executive Committee nor the candidates of BGMEA election 2007-2008 nor the General Body of BGMEA or its members were parties to the suit. Defendant No. 6 appealed against the order dated 11-3-2007 passed in the Suit in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 84 of 2007 which was allowed by the 6th Court of learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka by its order dated 5-6-2007. The plaintiff filed a revisional application being Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007 before this Court whereupon a Rule was issued and the operation of the order appealed against was stayed.

5. The Election Appeal Board passed an order on 3-7-2007 upholding the inclusion of the BGMEA representatives in the final voter list by the Election Board. Against the decision of the order of the Election Appeal Board, the respondent No. 6 filed an Appeal before respondent No.2, the Arbitration Tribunal. In that Appeal, the respondent No. 6 prayed for setting aside the order dated, 3-7-2007 and cancelling the nominations made by BGMEA in the FBCCI election 2007-2009 as evident in Annexure-'I' By the impugned order dated 25-9- 2007, the Arbitration Tribunal allowed the prayer of respondent No.6, directing exclusion of all the five nominees of BGMEA from the voter list of the FBCCI.

6. Feeling aggrieved by the order/award dated 25-9-2007, the petitioners obtained this Rule from this Court. On the date of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the impugned order/award was stayed for a period of three weeks from date. The order of stay was subsequently extended from time to time.

7. Respondent No. 1 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of respondent No. 1, in short, is that there is no express bar either in the Ordinance or in the Rules to challenging the legality of the decision of FBCCI Election Appeal Board before the Arbitration Tribunal. Section 12 of the Ordinance gives wide powers to the Tribunal to decide any questions or impropriety relating to election and is expressly made applicable to the present situation. By virtue of Article 13A of the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the FBCCI is legally entitled to reject the nominations of BGMEA and holding the election. Since the validity of BGMEA election is in dispute, the FBCCI is empowered by its Articles of Association to reject the nominations made by BGMEA. FBCCI is an apex trade organisation and is not concerned with the internal affairs/disputes of the members of BGMEA. The dispute relating to the BGMEA election is an internal matter strictly between the members of BGMEA. The FBCCI is not a party to the dispute. The Tribunal is empowered by its Articles to co-opt anyone person from the general members representing BGMEA if the latter fails to file nomination for the post of a nominated director.

8. Respondent No. 2 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of respondent No. 2, in short, is that the Arbitration Tribunal passed its judgment in accordance with law. It is also stated that the present Writ Petition is not maintainable as it is an unlawful fetter on the statutory obligations of the FBCCI as the apex trade organisation and it is unjustified in all the circumstances of the case advanced by the petitioners in this petition. It is important to mention here that the statements made in its affidavit-in-opposition by this respondent are almost identical to those in the affidavit of respondent No. 6 (FBCCI).

9. Respondent No. 6 also filed an affidavit-in- opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of this respondent, in short, is that on the date of filing of the suit the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) praying for temporary injunction restraining the principal defendants from holding of BGMEA election 2007- 2008. After hearing the plaintiff, the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka directed the principal defendants to show cause as to why an order of temporary injunction should not be granted within one day from the date of receipt of the notice. On 20-2-2007, the plaintiff filed another application under section 151 of the Code praying for an order of ad interim injunction restraining the principal defendants from holding BGMEA election scheduled to be held on 25-2-2007. Since the defendant did not appear within the time prescribed by the Court the learned Assistant Judge passed an order restraining the principal defendants from holding the election scheduled for 25-2-2007. In spite of the order of injunction, the election was held on 25-2-2007. Afterwards, the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) of the Code for wilful violation of the Court's order of injunction in Violation Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2007. On 27-7-2007, the plaintiff again filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code praying for an injunction restraining the principal defendant Nos. 5-6 from handing over their executive power to the Board of Directors. The learned Assistant Judge directed the principal defendants to show cause within five days. Since the defendant failed to appear, the learned Assistant Judge passed an order restraining the principal defendants from holding AGM on 12-3-2007. On 4-3-2007, defendant No.7 filed written objection against the application filed under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code. They also filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code for rejection of the plaint. Defendant No.6 appealed against the order dated 11-3-2007 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The Appeal ultimately was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka, who allowed the appeal setting aside the order of injunction passed by the learned Assistant Judge. The plaintiff then filed a revisional application being Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007 before this Court. The High Court Division issued Rule and stayed operation of the impugned judgment and order. Because of the pendency of the Civil Suit, the very locus standi of the persons nominated for the election of FBCCI is in dispute and, as such, the Arbitration Tribunal legally allowed the appeal.

10. Mr Rokanuddin Mahmud, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits as follows:

(1) The petmoner does not have the locus standi to file the Arbitration Appeal No. 14 of 2007 before the Arbitration Tribunal of FBCCI as he was not a member of FBCCl.

(2) In Arbitration Appeal No. 14 of 2007, BGMEA, a member body, was not made a party and as such, the order/award passed by the Tribunal is not binding on BGMEA.

(3) The findings of the Tribunal that the election of BGMEA was held in violation of the order of injunction dated 22-2-2007 is erroneous before disposal of Violation Miscellaneous. Case No. 16 of 2007. Unless the Violation Case is allowed, it cannot be said that the election was held in violation of the order of injunction.

(4) The order of injunction dated 11-3-2007 restraining the defendants from holding the AGM and from handing over power was also erroneous because before coming to such a finding, the civil Court must come to a finding that handing over power was made in violation of the order of injunction.

11. Mr Ajmalul Hossain, learned Advocate for respondent No.1, on the other hand, submits:

1. It is the duty of every citizen to abide by the lawful order passed by any Court and that showing respect to the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, the Arbitration Tribunal came to a finding that the election of BGMEA was held in violation of the order of injunction and that the AGM and the handing over power were also made in violation of the Court's order.

2. Under section 12 of the Ordinance any member of any trade organisation may file an Arbitration Case before the Arbitration Tribunal of FBCCI and in the instant case respondent No. 6 being a member of BGMEA was legally entitled to file the Arbitration Case before the Tribunal as mentioned above.

3. An interpretation of Article 14(1) of the Memorandum and Articles of Association of FBCCI is called for as the Board of Directors could not hand over power because of the order of stay passed by this Court.

12. Mr Tanjib-ul-Alam, learned Advocate for respondent No.2, submits as follows:

1. The Tribunal has exercised the power under section 12 of the Ordinance and that the findings made in the order/award were in accordance with law.

2. Though FBCCI was not made a party in the Arbitration Tribunal Case even then it is bound by order/award given by the Tribunal because the petitioners represent the BGMEA.

13. Mr SN Goswami, learned Advocate for respondent No. 6, submits as under:

1. The election of FBCCI is under dispute and, as such, the Arbitration Tribunal came to a finding that the persons nominated by the FBCCI could not be the voters of the election of FBCCI.

2. The election of FBCCI and holding of AGM and handing over powers were done in violation of two orders of injunction and unless those orders are set aside by a competent Court, the persons nominated by BGMEA in the FBCCI cannot be the voters of the election of FBCCl.

14. We have perused the Writ Petition and its annexures, the affidavits-in-opposition filed by respondent Nos.1, 2 and 6 and their annexures.

15. The preliminary voter list of BGMEA Election 2007 was published on 16-1-2007. The date for filing objection against the voter list was scheduled for 31-1-2007. The date of hearing objection was scheduled for 16-2-2007. The final list was published on 20-2-2007. On 20-2-2007, Mr Jahangir Alam filed Title Suit No. 53 of 2007 in the 4th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka praying for two reliefs as under.

"(a) a decree be passed declaring the final voter list published on 20-2-2007 for the Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) is void, illegal, erroneous, fraudulent, collusive, without jurisdiction, contrary to the rules and procedure for election of BGMEA null and void.

(b) a decree for permanent injunction restraining the principal defendants from holding election of BGMEA 2007-2008 scheduled to be held on 25-2-2007 and holding of further election on the basis of wrongful, fraudulent, collusive, illegal voter list published on 20-2- 2007."

Curiously enough, BGMEA was not made a defendant to the suit as evident in Annexure-C, the plaint of Title Suit No. 53 of 2007.

16. On 22-2-2007, the learned Assistant Judge restrained respondent Nos. 1-6 by an order of injunction from holding BGMEA election scheduled to be held on 25-2-2007. The BGMEA election was, however, held on 25-2-2007. A Miscellaneous Case filed by the plaintiff for violation of the order of injunction under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) of the Code on 27-2-2007 has been pending. On 11-3- 2007, the plaintiff filed another application for injunction restraining the defendants from holding AGM and from transferring power to the elected committee. The application for injunction was allowed as prayed for on that date. The AGM was, however, held and the power was transferred. On 15-3-2007, the plaintiff filed an application for withdrawal of the suit along with other Miscellaneous Cases filed by him. On 25-3-2007, respondent No. 3 filed an application to be added as a plaintiff and the application for addition was allowed. On 26-5-2007, notice inviting trade organisations to nominate members to the general body of the FBCCI for its election scheduled for 16-8-2007 was issued. On 25-6-2007, the preliminary voter list for FBCCI election was published. On 30-6-2007, respondent No. 6 filed an objection to the FBCCI Election Board seeking exclusion of the voters nominated by BGMEA. The appeal was rejected whereupon respondent No.6 filed Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007 before the Arbitration Tribunal of FBCCI. The Tribunal allowed the appeal directing exclusion of all five members nominated by BGMEA from the voter list of FBCCI.

17. The Tribunal came to a finding that the election of BGMEA was held in clear violation of the order of stay dated 20-2-2007. This finding of the Tribunal is erroneous on the ground that whether the election was held in violation of the order of stay (in fact, injunction) will be decided in Violation Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2007. Unless and until the Violation Case is allowed after taking evidence from both the sides, it is premature to say that the election was held in violation of the order of stay dated 22-2-2007. In addition, a Violation Case under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) is a quasi criminal proceedings which will only be decided upon taking evidence from both the sides.

18. Against the order of injunction dated 13-3-2007 restraining the defendants from holding AGM and from transferring executive power till disposal of the suit, defendant No. 7 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 84 of 2007 which was allowed. Against the judgment passed in the Appeal, the plaintiff filed a revisional application before this Court, which issued Rule and stayed the operation of the order passed by the appellate Court in Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007. The Arbitration Tribunal found that the current Executive Committee of BGMEA had been formed without lawful authority and that since the BGMEA Election had taken place in violation of a Court's order and was illegal, the Executive Committee formed by the Board of Directors pursuant to the BGMEA Election was illegal. This finding is also totally misconceived, because whether the Election had taken place in violation of the Court's order could not be decided by the Tribunal which even did not have the jurisdiction to say that the BGMEA Election had taken place in violation of the Court's order until the violation case is allowed and the suit is decreed. Had there been an order of injunction restraining exclusion of the nominations made by BGMEA from being voters of the FBCCI Election, the Tribunal in that event could exclude the voters of the BGMEA. It is contended that the holding of AGM and handing over executive power were not proper during continuance of the order of stay passed by the High Court Division. Whether the AGM and handing over power were done in violation of the order of stay passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007 may be decided in an appropriate proceeding if initiated by the plaintiff-petitioner. The interpretation of the Court's orders by the Tribunal regarding stay and injunction is erroneous and contrary to established principles of law.

19. Now the question is, whether the petitioner could file Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007 before the Arbitration Tribunal. Before adjudicating upon this point, let us have a glimpse over section 12 of the Ordinance as under:

"12. Restriction on suits against trade organisation-(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force or in the articles or memorandum of a registered trade organisation, no suit or other legal proceedings shall be instituted or commenced against such registered trade organisation ( or any member thereof or any member of the Executive Committee of such trade organisation) questioning the validity or propriety of any act or proceeding of such trade organisation or of the Executive Committee or other body thereof, or the constitution of, or election or appointment to, such Committee or body, by any member of such trade organisation or by any member of any other trade organisation unless such member or other trade organisation has made an application, accompanied by such fee not less than one thousand Taka as may be prescribed by rules, referring the matter to the Arbitration Tribunal constituted for the purpose of deciding such references by the Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry registered under the Act in pursuance of a licence and such Arbitration Tribunal has given its decision or award thereon.

(2) The Arbitration Tribunal constituted under sub-section (1) shall consist of not less than three and not more than five members appointed by the said Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry and shall conduct its proceedings and give its decision or award in accordance with the rules made in this behalf.

(3) Nothing in this section shall affect any suit or other legal proceedings instituted or commenced before the commencement of this Ordinance. "

20. From section 12 it appears that validity or propriety of any act or proceeding of a trade organisation or of the Executive Committee or other body thereof or the constitution of, or election or appointment to, such committee or body, by any member of such trade organisation or by any member of, or any other trade organisation cannot be challenged unless such member or other trade organisation has made an application to the Arbitration Tribunal.

21. The present dispute is relating to the election of FBCCI and not the election of BGMEA.

22. The meaning of the word 'member' must be construed with reference to Memorandum and Articles of Association of FBCCI. Article 1 (v) defines 'Member Body' which means Chamber of Commerce and/or Industry or an Association of trade and/or Industry which is an Ordinary Member of the Federation.

23. Article 4 states that every Chamber of Commerce and/or Industry or Association of Trade and/or Industry licensed by the Government and registered under section 26 of the Companies Act, 1913 shall be eligible to become Member of the Federation.

24. Article 10 provides that of Member Body shall cease to be a member of the Federation if the Board of Directors so decides in the event of non- payment of Annual Subscription within the period specified in that behalf or on derecognition or deregistration of the Member Body by the Government.

25. Article 13(i) provides that the General Body of the Federation shall consist of the General Members to be nominated by the Member Bodies for a particular term and such nominated Members of the General Body only shall be entitled to vote or contest in the election or nominate candidates for election and attend General Meetings. The number of General Members to be nominated by each Member Body shall be as follows:

"A" Class Chamber-6

"B" Class Chamber-4

"A" Class Association-5

"B" Class Association-3

26. Article 41 provides that a notice may be served upon any member either personally or by sending it through the post under Certificate of Posting in a pre-paid letter addressed to such Member at such Member's registered address. Any notice sent by post shall be deemed to have been served at the time when the letter containing the same would have been delivered in the ordinary course of post.

27. If the aforesaid Articles are considered in juxtaposition, it appears that FBCCI has two types of members (1) Ordinary Member/Member Body (2) General Members to be nominated by the member bodies. Now it is to be seen whether respondent No.6 Mahbub Minhaj is a member of FBCCI or not. Admittedly, respondent No. 6 was not nominated by the BGMEA (Member Body/Ordinary Member) to the General Body of the Federation to be its general member. 'Such member' occurring in section 12 of the Ordinance in the context of the present case for the purpose of challenging FBCCI Election shall mean and include only the members of FBCCI and none else. Therefore, respondent No. 6 did not have the locus standi to file Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007. It is important to note here that the definition of member may vary from one trade organisation to another trade organisation. Respondent No. 6 may be a member of BGMEA but not a member of FBCCI. Again, he being a member of BGMEA could challenge its voter list before the Arbitration Tribunal but not against voter list of FBCCI of which he is neither an ordinary member nor a general member.

28. Another important aspect is that respondent No.6 filed Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of2007 without impleading BGMEA as a party although BGMEA is an ordinary member of FBCCI. Before the Tribunal, BGMEA is the most aggrieved party because its nominations were under challenge, before the Tribunal. In this connection, reliance may be made in the case of Md Abdul Naim vs Chairman, Board of Directors, Sonali Bank 1 MLR (AD) 106 = 1 BLC (AD) 80. It is held as follows:

"The petitioner was in the service of Sonali Bank and his cause of action is against his employer and not against his appointing authority or appellate authority. They are merely functionaries of his employer. He may or may not make his appointing authority or appellate authority a party to the application under section 4(2), but it is obligatory for him to make his employer a party to the application or else any decree in his favour will be inexecutable."

29. Similar principle can be applied to the case in hand because the most aggrieved party BGMEA was not made a party to Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007. Therefore, we are of the view that BGMEA is not bound by the order/award passed by the Tribunal. In addition, though the facts of the case of Abdur Rashid vs Abdul Barik, 35 DLR (AD) 162 are distinguishable from those of the case in hand, the principle enunciated in the former case may be looked into. In that case, it is held that if a party satisfies a Court that summons were not duly served upon' him, the Court is bound to set aside the ex parte decree. In such a case. question of knowledge is not at all relevant and the ex parte decree will be set aside even if the defendant had knowledge of institution of the suit.

30. In the case in hand, BGMEA stated to have filed an application for addition of party and for adjournment on 25-9-2007. Respondent No. 2 (Arbitration Tribunal) in its affidavit-in-opposition stated "But since the Tribunal felt that BGMEA's adjournment application did not make any material difference on the issue before them and/or decision of the Tribunal, it rejected BGMEA's application for adjournment." The nomination made by the BGMEA was under challenge and therefore, its presence was indispensable before the Tribunal. But keeping the application for addition of party pending the Arbitration Tribunal passed the impugned order/award. From the above, it seems reasonably clear now that the haste precluded reasonable and deliberate judicial treatment of the case and was not warranted.

31. It is interesting to note here that respondent No. 2 (The Arbitration Tribunal) entered appearance in the case and contested it by filing an affidavit-in- opposition. It is not desirable that the Arbitration Tribunal supports its judgment or supports the case of the party in whose favour the award/order was passed. Arbitration Tribunal was made a party as a matter of practice. We disapprove of such a move of the Arbitration Tribunal. The rationale being that a Judge cannot defend his own judgment/decision.

32. Rule 16 of the Trade Organisation Rules, 1995 provides that if anybody has any objection regarding inclusion or deletion of the name of any person in the voter list, objection has to be filed within 6(six) days of publication of the voter list and that Appeal Board shall dispose of such objection within 3(three) days after hearing the parties. Therefore, it seems that finality has been attached to the decision of the Appeal Board. In the context of the present case, the Arbitration Tribunal should not have interfered with the decision of Appeal Board to which statutory finality has been attached. In the case in hand, the Arbitration Tribunal should have confined itself with FBCCI Election and not with BGMEA Election. If the election process is allowed to be thwarted at every stage, there will be no end of it.

33. Mr Ajmalul Hossain, learned Advocate, submits that interpretation of Article 14(i) is necessary in the context of the case in hand to determine whether the President and others of the Board of Directors had any responsibility in not holding the election in time. Article 14(iv) runs as under:

"14(iv) If the Board of Directors fails to take steps for holding election in time according to Article 14(ii), the President, the Vice- President and other members of the Board of Directors shall not be eligible to become candidates in the elections of the Board of Directors for the next two eligible terms."

<u>34. In the case in hand, the election could not be held because of the order of stay passed by the Court on 30-9-2007. Therefore, the President, the Vice-President and other members of the Board of Directors did not have any role in not holding the election within the stipulated time. As a result, they cannot be penalised for not holding the election within time. Therefore, disability mentioned in sub- article (iv) of Article 14 shall not apply to them.</u>

35. The findings made by the Arbitration Tribunal are, no doubt, erroneous but it cannot be said that it acted in a mala fide way.

In the light of the findings made above, we find substance in this Rule Nisi. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute and order/award (Annexure-A) is declared to have been passed without lawful authority having no legal effect. The order of stay passed at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated. There is no order as to costs,

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated May 28, 1998 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.364 of 1996).
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: The appeal by leave is against the judgment dated May 28, 1998 of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.364 of 1996 making the Rule absolute. The revisional application was filed against the judgment and order dated November 13, 1995 of the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in Arbitration Appeal No.43 of 1994 allowing the appeal and thereby setting aside the award dated September 18, 1994 of the Arbitrator (appointed under section 27 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982) in Arbitration Revision Case No.1636 of 1990 and sending the Arbitration Revision case to the Court of the Arbitrator to dispose of the Arbitration revision case upon hearing the parties.

2. It may be mentioned the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal set aside the judgment and order of the Arbitrator on the finding that the Arbitrator passed the award in the arbitration revision case awarding award for an amount which was more than 10% of the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner in respect of the land acquired belonging to the respondents. The Arbitration Appellate Tribunal set aside the award made by the Arbitrator, upon placing reliance on the provision of section 31 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. 11 of 1982), hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance, on the view that the amount awarded by the Arbitrator was more than 10% of the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner. It may be mentioned award was made in the Arbitration Revision Case No.1636 of 1990 on September 18, 1994, i.e. at a time when the Arbitrator could make award of the amount as in his view in the facts and circumstance of the case proper i.e. it was not the law that Arbitrator could only make award to extent of 10% over the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner. The provision of law putting the embargo on the power of the Arbitrator to award amount not exceeding 10% on the award already made by the Deputy Commissioner was made by the amending Act No.20 of 1994 upon adding a proviso to section 31 of the Act. The said Act No.20 of 1994 was published in the Bangladesh Gazette (Ordinary) on 1st of December, 1994. The amending Act was prospective one. This being the position the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal was in error in setting aside the award made by the Arbitrator on September 18, 1994 on the view that the said award was made in violation of section 31 of the Ordinance ie. amount awarded exceeded 10% of the award made by the Deputy Commissioner.

3. As against the order of the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal the respondents moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule in the aforementioned revisional case. It was contended by the respondents herein before the High Court Division that the date on which award was made by the Arbitrator there was no law putting embargo on the power of the Arbitrator in making the award exceeding 10% on the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner. It was further contended since the law putting embargo on the power of the Arbitrator in making award exceeding 10% of the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner came into operation on December 1, 1994 and that the Arbitrator as passed the award on September 18, 1994, the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal was in error in setting aside the award made by the Arbitrator.

4. Before the High Court Division it was submitted on behalf of the Appellant Nos.1 and 2 that as the appeal has not been disposed of on merit, the High Court Division should send back the appeal to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal for disposal on merit.

5. So, it is seen that the opposite party before the High Court Division, i.e. the appellants herein, did not dispute the contention of the petitioner before the High Court Division, i.e. the respondents herein, that Arbitration Appellate Tribunal was wrong in setting aside the award made by the Arbitrator on the view that the Arbitrator made the award exceeding 10% over the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner since law putting embargo on the power of the Arbitrator to make award exceeding 10%' on the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner came into force on December 1, 1994.

6. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute and thereupon set aside the judgment and order of the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal on the finding that the contention made by the petitioners i.e. the respondents herein, was of merit i.e. the law putting embargo on the power of the Arbitrator in making award not exceeding 10% over the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner come into force on a date later than the date of award made by the Arbitrator i.e. the law came into operation on December 1, 1994, but the award was made on September 18, 1994.

7. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division did not find merit in the contention of the appellants, who were opposite parties before the High Court Division, that the case may be sent back to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal since the said appeal was not disposed of on merit.

8. Leave was granted to consider the contention of the appellants that the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal dismissed the Arbitration revision case on the view that the Arbitrator made the award awarding amount exceeding 10% of the amount awarded by the Deputy Commissioner and that as the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal did not dispose of the appeal on merit and that High Court Division having had held that the view taking which the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal allowed the appeal and sent back the revisional arbitration case to the Court of Arbitrator for disposal afresh was not correct, the said Division was in error in not remanding the appeal to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal for disposal on merit or, in other words, to decide the case on consideration of the materials brought on record by the award holders in support of their claim of revision of the award made by the Deputy Commissioner.

9. We have heard the learned Advocates-on- Record for the appellants as well as for the respondent No.1 and perused. the materials on record. It is seen from the judgment of the Arbitrator that the Arbitrator considered the judgment made in the Arbitration revision case filed in connection with the acquisition of land in LA Case No.13 of 1987- 88. In the said LA case, land of plot No.131 0 was acquired and the nature of the land was nal. In the said arbitration revision case the Arbitrator fixed the price of per acre of nal land at Taka 55 lac. From the side of the appellants no material was placed before the Arbitrator to show that the award made in the Arbitration revision cases which were filed in connection with the acquisition of land of plot No.1310 upon starting LA Case No.13 of 1987-88, was set aside or modified by the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal or by higher Court. It may be mentioned respondents land was in Matuail Mouza i.e. of the Mouza land whereof was acquired in LA Case No. 13 of 1987-88 and the land so acquired in said LA case was nal land ie. class of land as was of the respondents. The land of the respondents was acquired upon initiating LA Case No.l3 of 1987-88 and the quantity of the land so acquired was 17 decimals and the land so acquired was of Plot No.3979 and the class of land was nal. The Arbitrator having found that the award revision cases filed in connection with the acquisition of land in LA Case No. 13 of 1987-88 were disposed of fixing the value at Taka 50,00,000 per acre of nal land and that the land acquired belonging to the respondents being of the same Mouza as well as being of the same class and also of the same nature held that the Deputy Commissioner while making the award deprived the owners of the legitimate value of the land to which they were entitled. The Arbitrator, in the background of the fact as stated hereinbefore, fixed the price of per acre of nal land at Taka 50,00,000 and thereupon awarded Taka 8,50,000 for the acquired land i.e. 17 decimals of nal land and the statutory compensation Taka 1,73,000, in total Taka 10,23,000. Since the respondent earlier received compensation of Taka 2,73,964, the Arbitrator upon deducting the said amount made an award of Taka 7,26,000.

10. It was contended before the Arbitrator that the arbitration revision case was barred by limitation and that the same was not maintainable since the respondents, ie. affected persons, without protest received the amount earlier awarded by the Deputy Commissioner. The Arbitrator held that the arbitration revision case was filed within time as prescribed by law and also held that arbitration revision case was quite maintainable since filing of the very arbitration revision case manifestly demonstrates that the persons in whose favour Deputy Commissioner made the award were not agreeable to the amount so awarded by the Deputy Commissioner and, as such, it cannot be said that withdrawal of the money awarded by the Deputy Commissioner, is to be construed, that the affected persons accepted the award made by the Deputy Commissioner without protest. It may be mentioned that when a person whose land was acquired and the Deputy Commissioner awards compensation for said acquired land files a revision award case that itself can sufficiently be considered that the affected person did not accept the award made by the Deputy Commissioner as correct and thereupon having been aggrieved filed the revision award case, in that state of the matter it cannot be said that money awarded by the Deputy Commissioner for the acquired land was received by the affected persons without protest.

<u>11. The contention upon making which the leave was obtained would have been the good grounds for allowing the appeal and sending revision award case back to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal for disposal of the appeal on merit, if the appellants would have filed any material before the Arbitrator in rebuttal of the materials brought on record by the respondents in support of their case before the Arbitrator. It is seen from the judgment of the Arbitrator that respondents land as well as some other land was acquired upon starting LA Case No.13 of 1987-88. The affected persons of the LA Case No.13 of 1987-88 other than the respondents filed some arbitration revision case questioning the correctness of the award made by the Deputy Commissioner. The Arbitrator in those revision cases fixing the value of per acre of the nal land at Taka 50,00,000 made the award. No material was placed on the record from the side-of the appellants before the Arbitrator to show that the award made in the arbitration revision cases fixing value of the na11and of Mouza Matuail per acre at Taka 50,00,000 was revised on appeal by the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal or by the superior Court. This being the position we are of the view that no error was committed by the High Court Division in not sending back the appeal to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal while making the Rule absolute. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view no useful purpose would be served in sending back the appeal to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal for disposal afresh and as such we do not find any merit in the contention made by the appellants for sending back the appeal to the Arbitration Appellate Tribunal.</u>

12. In view of the discussions made hereinabove we find no merit in the appeal.

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed with cost to be paid by the appellant No.1.

End.

full_judgment:
SM Hossain J: Writ Petition Nos. 1448 of 2008 and 3071 of 2008 having been heard together are disposed of by this common judgment as they involve common questions of law and facts. In both the Writ Petitions the petitioners challenged the LA Case No. 1/2007-2008 to be illegal and without lawful authority.

2. The facts of Writ Petition No.1448 of2008, in brief, are:

Because of increase of population and vehicles in Dhaka City Corporation (in short, DCC), the Government imposed restrictions on plying trucks within the city from morning to 8-00/9-00 PM As a result, the members of English Road Iron and Steel Merchants Association (in short, the Association) have been facing serious problems in carrying on their business. The Association through the petitioner had been looking for a piece of land at Jatrabari area of DCC in order to set up godowns for its members with sufficient space for loading and unloading of trucks within the area of their godowns. After extensive search, the petitioner found out the land measuring an area of 1041 acres in that area. A total of 119 members of the Association became interested in purchasing land in their own names but to use that land jointly for the business. The purchase was made as back as in 1988. The members of the Association initially set up godowns for storing commodities in the purchased land and also had been giving delivery 01' bulk sale from there by unloading and loading trucks. They established shops on that land and ultimately, turned it into a market. The market bears a signboard, which reads "English Road Iron and Steel Merchants Association Jatrabari Market". The Association purchased land from RS plot No. 2357 corresponding to Mahanagar survey plot Nos. 4943 and 4945 and those two plots are contiguous to a vast vacant land of Mahan agar Survey plot NoA805. Mahanagar Survey plot Nos. 4951, 4994, 4999, 5000, 5001, 5002 and 5003 are situated by the side of Dhaka-Chittagong highway where a wholesale market for vegetables has been functioning. Plot No. 5003 is contiguous to plot No. 4805. All of a sudden, the petitioner came to know about the service of a notice dated 12-7-2007 under the signature of respondent No.6 on behalf of respondent No. 7 under section 3 of The Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (in short, the Ordinance). The notice was served on Mr A Samad, an owner of the land recorded in RS plot No. 2357. The notice disclosed the intention of the Government for acquisition of 5 acres of land from RS plot No. 2357. The total quantum of the land of RS plot No. 2357 is 11.08 acres. Respondent No. 6 also affixed a notice under section 3 of the Ordinance on the notice board of respondent No.3 mentioning RS plot No. 2357 and two others. After perusal of the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance, the petitioner found that though proposal was made for acquiring land from RS Plot No. 2357, description of the land to be acquired was vague and indefinite for not specifying the boundaries of 5 acres out of 11.08 acres of land of that plot. As soon as the petitioner came to know about the notice, he submitted objection to respondent No. 3 stating details and praying for excluding the land of the Association from the proposal of acquisition as the land was being used for public purpose. As there is no response against the objection from respondent No.3, the petitioner on 9-9-2007 submitted another objection to respondent No. 2. Hearing the objection, respondent No.3 assured the petitioner of consideration of his prayer after obtaining a report from the concerned officers about the existence of the vast vacant area of land of Plot No.4805 adjacent to the land proposed to be acquired. On 14-11-2007, the Association received a notice dated 12-11-2007 under section 6 of the Ordinance from respondent No. 6, on behalf of respondent No. 3, directing the members of the Samity to appear before him and for giving statements about their interest in the property and fixing the next date for 25-11-2007. Respondent No.6 on behalf of respondent No.3 issued another notice dated 5-2-2008 under section 7 of the Ordinance upon each of the members who purchased the land described in the schedule to the Writ Petition. The members of the Association are still in possession of the land in question and have been carrying on business there. Since the petitioner failed to impress upon the concerned authority to release the disputed land from acquisition, he filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained this Rule Nisi.

3. In Writ Petition No.3071 of 2008, the facts, in brief, are:

The petitioner purchased .64 acre of land of mouza Jatrabari, PS Demra from the successor-in- interest of RS recorded owner Mr Alauddin by the registered deed of sale dated 6-3-2000. The purchased land appertains to CS plot No. 597 under CS Khatian No.118, SA plot No.597, under SA khatian No.294 and RS plot No.2357 under RS Khatian No. 57. The petitioner got his name mutated both in the RS and SA khatians. While the petitioner was in possession of the land in question, the officials of DCC came to evict him on 3-4-2008 stating that the land was acquired by respondent No. 1 for the purpose of development of Jatrabari Wholesale Kachcha Bazar of DCC. The petitioner was taken aback as no notice was served upon him under sections 3, 5, 6 and 7 of the Ordinance. The petitioner filed an application to the Mayor, DCC for releasing his 0.64 acre of land from acquisition proposal. In reply to the application, the DCC stated that the land in question was acquired by respondent No.1 after complying with the provisions of law as evidenced by Annexure-C 1 dated 10-4-2008. On query, the petitioner came to know that notices under sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Ordinance were not issued/served upon the petitioner in LA Case No. 1 of 2007-2008. Without executing any agreement according to section 15(1) of the Ordinance, the LA case was started. Notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance were not served upon the petitioner though his name was duly mutated in RS khatian No.57, vide Mutation Nothi No. 11205 of 2004 and Mutation Khatian No. 1716. The existing Kacha Bazar has been developed almost wholly on the khas land earlier used by DCC as garbage dumping station. Of total 11.08 acres of land of RS plot No. 2357, an area measuring 6.30 acres is the khas land of the Government. On 3-4-2008, the officials of DCC went to the location and demarcated the area by hoisting red flags at four points covering partial Kachcha Bazar and partial Iron and Steel Market. Only 5.0102 acres of land have been proposed for acquisition for the development of Kacha Bazar but no specific demarcation of the proposed land was mentioned in the notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance. The petitioner collected a notice which revealed that the Assistant Commissioner (Land) took step for recovery of the khas land measuring 6.30 acres of RS plot No.2357. Respondent No. 9 issued a letter to the Deputy Commissioner by memo dated 25-5-1998 informing the decision of the National Economic Committee regarding (1) the use of Government khas land in implementing the development project and directing the Deputy Commissioner to use khas land first, failing which, they can acquire land, (2) video recording of the location of the proposed project. As per provisions of section 15(1) of the Ordinance, an agreement between the acquiring authority and the requiring body is mandatory before issuance of notice under section 3 in respect of the property proposed to be acquired for any person other than the Government. Failing to impress upon the concerned authority to release the land from acquisition, the petitioner obtained this Rule Nisi from this Court on 20-4-2008.

4. Respondent No. 3 filed affidavit-in-opposition in both the Writ Petitions. The identical stand of respondent No.3 in both the Writ Petitions is:

Under the Ordinance, a total quantum of 5.211 acres of land of Mouza Jatrabari was proposed to be acquired on a proposal initiated by the DCC, the requiring body, for public purpose to set up a wholesale green vegetable market vide LA Case No. 1/2007-2008. Notice under section 3 was issued in accordance with law. After service 'Of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance upon the owners of the land in question, some of them raised objections before respondent No.3. The objections were heard by respondent No. 3 under section 4(1) of the Ordinance and he prepared a report under section 4(2) of the Ordinance. The report was sent to the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka, who gave final decision under section 5(1A) of the Ordinance. On 11-11-2007, notice under section 6 of the Ordinance was served and on 5-2-2008, notice for payment of compensation under section 7 of the Ordinance was accordingly served by the authorised officer. Subsequently, the acquired land was handed over to the requiring body on 14-2-2008. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) wrote a letter to the Deputy Controller, Bangladesh Forms and Publications, Tejgaon, Dhaka requesting the latter to publish a declaration under section 11(2) of the Ordinance in the official Gazette.

5. Respondent Nos. 4 and 5 filed affidavits- in-opposition in both the Writ Petitions. The case of respondent Nos. 4 and 5 is that according to the decision of the Government, the Dee undertakes to establish four wholesale green vegetable markets in different areas of Dee and that Dee is merely executing the decision of the Government.

6. Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008 submits as follows:

(1) Notice under section 3 of the Ordinance is defective. The land proposed to be acquired was not specified in the notice which was not even issued by a competent person according to that section.

(2) Notice under section 6 of the Ordinance was not properly served upon the members of the Association.

(3) Violating the provisions of the Ordinance, the land owned by the members of the Association was acquired.

(4) ভূমি প্রশাসন ম্যানুয়েল 2nd part provides that the land used for carrying on business should be kept outside the purview of acquisition when khas land is available. The proposal for acquiring land belonging to private individuals should be avoided. In the instant case, RS plot No. 2357 corresponding to Mohanagar Survey plot Nos. 4943 and 4945 measuring more than 11.08 acres belonging to the Government has been lying vacant and the proposed market can be established there.

(5) No agreement was entered into between the Government and Dee under section 3( 1) of the Ordinance and, as such, the very acquisition is illegal and without jurisdiction.

7. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 in addition to the grounds agitated by Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, submits that no notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance was served upon the petitioner and, as such, the proceeding of the impugned  LA Case so far as the petitioner concerned is illegal and without jurisdiction. He further submits that as per the map prepared by the acquiring authority, the land owned by the petitioner does not fall within it. He lastly submits that video recording was not made as per the Acquisition of Immovable Property Rules, 1982 (in short, the Rules).

8. The learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of respondent No. 3, on the other hand, submits that the acquisition in question was made after observing all legal formalities and, as such, there is nothing to interfere with acquisition proceeding. He further submits that meanwhile, Gazette notification had been published and, as such, the property vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. He then submits that the video recording of land proposed to be acquired was made 5 days after issuance of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance and that the video recording shows that all existing structures were intact and that the petitioner did not raise any objection as to demolition of any structure by the requiring body prior to video recording. He also submits that notice was served upon the vender of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 in accordance with law. He then submits that no agreement is required to be entered into between the Government and the DCC which is merely executing the decision of the Government for establishing four wholesale green vegetable markets in Dhaka City. In elaborating his submission, he states that DCC is under the Ministry of Local Government and DCC being a governmental organisation, no such agreement is required. He however, submits that later, Dee entered into an agreement with the Government and even if there is any defect, that was cured later.

9. Mr MA Baki, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 4 and 5, adopted the submissions made by the learned Deputy Attorney- General.

10. We have considered both the Writ Petitions and the affidavits-in-opposition, supplementary affidavits and the annexures thereto. The petitioners of both the Writ Petitions took serious exceptions that no notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was served upon them at all. In this connection, it is necessary to quote section 3 of the Ordinance as under:

"Whenever it appears to the Deputy Commissioner that any property in any locality is needed or is likely to be needed for any public purpose or in the public interest, he shall cause a notice to be published at convenient places on or near the property in the prescribed form and manner stating that the property is proposed to be acquired:

Provided that no property used by the public for the purpose of religious worship, graveyard and cremation ground shall be acquired."

11. From section 3, it appears that the notice is required to be published at convenient places on or near the property in the prescribed form and manner stating that the property is proposed to be acquired.

12. Therefore, section 3 of the Ordinance does not enjoin service of notice upon the owners of the land proposed to be acquired. In this context, reliance may be placed on the case of MA Salam vs Bangladesh 6 MLR (AD) 184, in which it was held that section 3 of the Ordinance does not provide for personal service of notice upon the owner of the land. It is provided for notice to be published on the property or near the property.

13. It is not the case of the petitioner that no such notice was at all published as required under section 3 of the Ordinance. They merely contend that notice under section 3 was not served upon them and such contention does not have any place within the four comers of the section. Similar view has also been taken in the case of Noel Gregory Mendes vs Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong 6 MLR (AD) 112.

14. The petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 took a serious exception that notice under section 6 was not at all served upon him, though he purchased the land in the year 2000 and his name was recorded in the RS and the SA khatians. Section 6 of the Ordinance is as follows:

"6( 1) When the Government, the Divisional Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner, as the case may be, has made a decision for acquisition of any property under section 5 or the proviso to section 4(3)(b), as the case may be, the Deputy Commissioner shall cause public notice to be given in the prescribed manner at convenient places on or near such property stating that the Government, the Divisional Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner, as the case may be, has decided to acquire the property and intends to take possession thereof and that claims for compensation for all with interests in such property may be made to him.

(2) Such notice shall state the particulars of the property to, be acquired and taken possession of, and shall require all persons interested in the property to appear personally or by agent before the Deputy Commissioner at a time, not being earlier than fifteen days after date of publication of the notice, and place mentioned therein and to state the nature of their respective interest in the property and the amount and particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests.

(3) The Deputy Commissioner shall also serve notice to the same effect in the prescribed from on the occupier if any of such property and on all persons known or believed to be interested therein."

15. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, however, submits that the petitioner does not reside in the case land as is evident from the cause title of the Writ Petition itself and that notices under sections 3 and 6 were served upon his vendor. It is, of course, true that as soon as land was sold to the petitioner, the vendor lost all his interest in the land. Let us see whether or not non service of such notice on the petitioner is fatal. Admittedly, the land of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 has been lying vacant. As per the cause title of the Writ petition, it appears that he resides at 121 Shantinagar, Dhaka at present 329/A/6 South Jatrabari, Dhaka.

16. In this regard, reliance may be placed on the case of Abdur Rouf Chowdhury vs Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land and Acquisition) 3 BLC 330 in which it is held that although the petitioners were interested in the property under acquisition, no notice was served upon them under section 6(3) of the Ordinance. This irregularity in the procedure will not ipso facto render the acquisition illegal provided that acquisition was for a public purpose and compensation amount was adequate and fixed in accordance with law.

17. The High Court Division came to the 'above finding on the question of non-service of notice under section 6 of the Ordinance. Therefore, it appears that non-service of notices under section 6 of the Ordinance is not fatal.

18. Identity of the land.

The notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance show that there is no specification of what quantum of land was being acquired from each of the plots proposed to be acquired. Before initiation of the acquisition process, the requiring body made a survey of the land proposed to be acquired and also its adjoining area. The map reveals that prior to issuing notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance, the land proposed to be acquired was clearly identified in map dated 21-5-2007 which was produced before the Court at the hearing of the Rule Nisi.

The petitioner of Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008 and the members of the petitioner's association did not raise any objection about the vagueness of the land proposed to be acquired as evidenced by Annexures-C and D series. In passing, a reference may be made to the case of Mizanur Rahman (Md) vs Deputy Commissioner. Mymensingh 7 BLC (AD) 17 in which it is held:

"After having heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner the learned Judge of the High Court Division said that no such question (vagueness) was raised before the acquisition authority and accordingly, found no substance in the contention."

Therefore, the contention as to vagueness of the land proposed to be acquired falls through.

19. Availability of khas land near the land proposed to be acquired is one of the main contentions of the petitioners. Serial No. 12 of ভূমি প্রশাসন ম্যান্যুয়েল, ২য় খন্ড runs as under:

“ উল্লেখিত সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প বাস্তবায়নে সরকারি খাসজমি ব্যবহারকে সর্বোচ্চ অগ্রাধিকার প্রদান করিতে হইবে। খাসজমি প্রাপ্তি সম্ভব না হইলে জমি অধিগ্রহনের কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করিতে হইবে।

অধিগ্রহণ প্রস্তাবে কৃষি জমি বা অন্য কোন মূল্যবান জমি থাকিলে উহা সম্ভব বাদ দিয়া তৎপরিবর্তে অনাবাদী, পতিত বা কম মূল্যবান জমি অধিগ্রহনের প্রচেষ্ঠা গ্রহণ করিতে হইবে। ইহা ছাড়া ঘনবসতি এলাকা, শিল্প এলাকা, ব্যবসা-বানিজ্য এলাকা, শিক্ষা ও সামাজিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের জন্য ব্যবহৃত সম্পত্তি ও যথাসম্ভব পরিহার করিতে হইবে।”

20. It is contended on behalf of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 that an area of land measuring 6.30 acres appertaining to RS plot No. 2357 is the khas land. The petitioner stated that the Assistant Commissioner (Land) issued a notice (Annexure-F) to the General Hospital (Private Limited) for recovery of khas land measuring 6.30 acres appertaining to RS plot No. 2357. The CS record shows that the land claimed to be the khas land belonged to a private individual. The SA khatian in respect of that land was, however, prepared in the name of the Government. The basis of preparation of SA khatian in the name of the Government could not be satisfactorily established by either party. In such a state of affairs, it cannot be conclusively said at this stage that the khas land standing in the name of the Government in RS khatian belongs to the Government. Annexure-F of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 shows that a private hospital is on a portion of that khas land. Since setting up of a vegetable market is very urgent, taking over possession of land belonging to the Government in occupation of somebody else may take time. Therefore, the contention that the wholesale green vegetable market can be set up on the khas land does not stand to reason.

21. It is contended that DCC being not a government organisation, the Government ought to have entered into an agreement with the former before issuance of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance. The petitioner relies upon the case of Sankar Gopal Chatterjee vs Additional Commissioner. Dhaka Division 41 DLR 326 in which it is held that:

"Before the Deputy Commissioner acquires the jurisdiction to publish a notice under section 3 an agreement with the non- Government requiring body is a sine qua non for the exercise of such power. It is a condition precedent. It cannot be whittled down by any device."

22. In the above case, the land was proposed to be acquired for Sub-Divisional Co-operative Multi-purpose Society Ltd, Kishoreganj, a private body engaged in profit earning businesses. In the instant case, DCC is part of the Local Government and it may be designated as governmental body. The supplementary affidavit filed by respondent Nos. 3-5 reveals that DCC is merely executing the decision of the Government by taking initiative to establish four wholesale green vegetable markets as evidenced by Annexure-3 to the supplementary affidavit.

23. Therefore, it appears that the Government has been implementing its decision through DCC.

24. In the case of Bangladesh vs Subash Chandra Das 46 DLR (AD) 63, while concurring with the author Judge, Mr Justice Mustafa Kamal observed as follows:

"Reading all the sections together, sections 8, 9, 10, 12 and 15, it is clear that abatement will take place if the acquiring authority fails to "pay" or "deposit" compensation in terms of section 10 within one year from the date of decision of the Government (which is section 5 in the case of acquisition). The requiring body, therefore, will deposit the consideration money with the Government well ahead of expiry of one year from the date of decision of the Government but within what date, is a subject matter of agreement between the Government and the requiring body under section IS. This is their internal arrangement, but legal consequence of abatement will follow only when the Government fails to 'pay' or 'deposit' compensation it terms of section 10."

25. From the above cited case, it appears that the agreement is an internal arrangement between the Government and the requiring body and the LA Case shall abate if the compensation money is not deposited within time.

26. In the instant case an agreement was . entered into between the Government and DCC after notice under section 3 was issued. But we are of the opinion that on the facts and in the circumstances of the instant case, no such agreement was necessary between the Government and the Dhaka City Corporation. Therefore, the case reported in 41 DLR 326 has no manner of application on the facts and in the circumstances of the present case.

27. While according approval, the Central Land Allocation Committee resolved as under:

“ ঢাকা শহরে ৪টি পাইকারী কাঁচাবাজার নির্মানের পরিকল্পনার আওতায় যাত্রাবাড়ী পাইকারী কাঁচাবাজার নির্মানের জন্য যাত্রাবাড়ী মৌজায় ব্যক্তি মালিকানাধীন ৫.২১১ একর জমি অধিগ্রহন প্রস্ত ? অনুমোদন করা হলো এবং বর্তমানে ব্যবসারতদের দোকান বরাদ্দের বিষয়টি নিশ্চিত করার সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হয় ”।

28. The above condition was appended while the Committee accorded approval to the acquisition of the land in question. Therefore, DCC is under the obligation to abide by the decision of the Central Land Allocation Committee, Consequently, as soon as the constructions of the wholesale green vegetable markets are completed, the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008 and the affected shop owners having admitted title to the acquired land will get first priority in the allotment of shops. DCC cannot deviate from the direction of the Central Land Allocation Committee.

29. Mr Prabir Halder, learned Advocate for the petitioners of Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008, submits that notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was not issued by a competent person and, as such, all actions taken in respect of acquisition of the land in question will fall through.

30. Admittedly, notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was issued under the signature of Mr Ishaque Mia, Additional Land Acquisition Officer and authorised officer on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 12-7-2007. It is, of course, true that Mr Md Ishaque Mia was under order of transfer when he issued the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance and he was succeeded by Mr Bibakananda Sarker who joined the Land Acquisition Section, Dhaka on 9-7 -2007 as evidenced by Annexure-11 to the affidavit-in-opposition filed in Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008. The learned Deputy Attorney- General submits that there are as many as nine branches in Land Acquisition Section, each branch is manned by an Additional Land Acquisition Officer. Amplifying his submission, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, submits that Mr Bibak- ananda Sarker joined in the LA section of Dhaka on 9-7-2007 but did not take charge of the 9th Branch of LA Section. Annexure-12 of the affidavit-in- opposition indicates that Mr Md Ishaque Mia made over charge of the 9th branch of the LA Section to Mr Bibakananda Sarker on 19-7-2007. Therefore, it is crystal clear that prior to 19-7-2007, Mr  Md Ishaque Mia was competent to issue notice under section 3 of the Ordinance. As a result, the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner does not hold good.

31. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate for the petitioner of Writ Petitioner No. 3071 of 2008, contends that the video recording of the land proposed to be acquired was not done according to the Acquisition of the Immovable Property Rules, 1982 (in short, the Rules) and, as such, the entire acquisition proceeding is illegal and without jurisdiction.

32. Let us have a glimpse over Rule 4A of the Rules as under:

"Video of the land proposed to be acquired -Immediately before publishing notice under section 3, a video of the land to be acquired shall be made along with all structures and trees thereon by the Deputy Commissioner in presence of the requiring person, local elites and elected representative of the Union or the Municipality within the local limits of which the land is situated."

<u>33. From the above Rule, it appears that the use of the word "immediately" prior to the words "before publishing notice under section 3 of the Ordinance" is very significant. Having considered the entire Rule, in general, we are of the opinion that video recording has to be done immediately before issuance of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance but not before taking decision of acquisition of the land. Therefore, in the decision-making process of acquisition, this Rule had no role to play. The petitioners are aggrieved by the decision of acquisition, not by the delay in video recording of the land.</u>

34. Admittedly, the video recording of the proposed land was made five days after the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was served. The learned Deputy Attorney-General produced the CD which contained the video recording of the land. The video recording shows that all the structures on the land were intact. The purpose of video recording is to see that the existing trees and structures on the land proposed to be acquired are intact for the purpose of determination of compensation of those structures and that any unscrupulous affected land owner cannot erect flimsy structures to claim compensation. The petitioners did not raise any grievance that the existing structures were not included in the video recording and that' compensation was not assessed for those structures.

35. Therefore, we are of the view that a delay of five days in video recording of the land is not fatal to render the entire acquisition proceeding illegal and without jurisdiction.

36. It is contended on behalf of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of2008 that the land of the petitioner does not fall within the land under acquisition and therefore, notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance was illegally issued in respect of the land of the petitioner.

<u>37. This contention does not have any force.</u>

<u>Whether or not the land of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 falls within the acquisition is a disputed question of fact and such question cannot be resolved without measurement and taking evidence which is beyond the purview of the writ jurisdiction.</u>

38. In the light of the findings made before, we do not like to interfere with the acquisition process.

39. In the result, the Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008 is disposed of and the respondents are directed to allot the shops to the affected shop owners having valid title to the acquired land on priority basis before giving allotment to others. The order of stay passed in Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008 is hereby recalled and vacated.

40. No order as to costs.

The Rule issued in Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.
